title: 2027 health reimbursement decree — price-discount indices force hospitals and specialists to buy centre drugs cheaper
money_note: No money is attached to the need. The decree governs a public health-insurance system with 2027 costs of 604.8bn CZK; the RIA puts the direct saving from the centre-drug price-discount indices at 2.2bn CZK and the best-practice purchasing gap at up to 7bn CZK. Those are savings estimates, not a budget, so they are not scored as money.
summary: The health ministry's draft reimbursement decree for 2027 applies price-discount indices to specialised centre drugs, splitting the average gap between hospitals' purchase costs and reported prices 55:45 in insurers' favour and cutting reimbursements by an estimated 2.2bn CZK. Its RIA finds that if every provider bought at best-practice prices the saving would reach 7bn CZK, and it tells out-of-hospital specialists to buy cheaper, alone, in groups or with hospitals, or to change their drug mix.
notes: STATUS: DRAFT — MZd decree in comment procedure (VeKLEP ALBSDXRFYLM6, '2 - v pripominkovem rizeni', authorised 2026-09-09, comments due 2026-09-23); the ministry must issue it every year under s. 17(5) of Act 48/1997 and it applies wherever an insurer and a provider do not agree otherwise. DATES: effect 1 January 2027 (materiál https://www.odok.cz/portal/services/download/attachment/KORNDXRKFD7V/ : 'Tato vyhláška nabývá účinnosti dnem 1. ledna 2027'). RIA 'Definice problému' (in the důvodová zpráva): the fee negotiation ran 29 Jan - 18 Jun 2026 and ended with agreement in 11 of 15 segments, a partial agreement for labs, and no agreement for acute inpatient, follow-up inpatient and specialised outpatient care. System 2027: revenue 605bn CZK (+44.4bn, 7.9%), costs 604.8bn (+28.4bn, 4.9%), balance +0.2bn; insurers' reserves fall from 43.2bn (end 2025) to an expected 33.2bn (end 2026). Centre drugs: weighted-average purchase gap about 4bn CZK, best-practice gap up to 7bn; indices from the joint negotiation proposal would have saved only 1.5bn; segment growth 2027/2026 put at 6.7% excluding the new Alzheimer drugs (up to 3.2bn, left to individual contracts). Sensitivity items: hip/knee endoprostheses moved to contract terms (possible saving about 2.2bn), e-lab requisitions, flu-vaccination bonus for hospital staff (1.3bn), late-reporting penalty kept at 95% for 2027 care reported after 31 March 2028. The URL is the důvodová zpráva attachment (KORNDXRKFEMB). DEDUP: veklep-KORNDXRFYLM6 (2026-09-19 ledger, metadata only) is the scripted-feed card; reg-mzd-uhradova-432-2025 is the 2026 decree. This record is the 2027 decree's dated substance and its quantified purchasing problem. Who must act: hospital pharmacies and purchasing departments, out-of-hospital dermatology and rheumatology specialists who give centre drugs, the insurers.

title: Housing-completion share of VAT for municipalities — MPs' bill to pay towns per m² of finished flats from 2028
money_note: The bill's own explanatory memorandum computes a mechanical transfer of 8.12-9.90bn CZK a year from 2024 completions (uncapped floor area) and says the real amount would be lower after the per-flat caps. It is a draft MPs' bill with no government position yet, so no money is scored.
summary: A deputies' bill (Chamber print 298) would amend the tax revenue sharing act so that municipalities receive 3,000-4,000 CZK and regions 500 CZK per m² of living area of flats completed on their territory in the previous year, paid from the state's share of VAT from 1 January 2028. Its explanatory memorandum argues that today's sharing rules give towns no direct fiscal reward for housing construction, although they carry the infrastructure costs up front, and sizes the transfer at 8.1-9.9bn CZK a year on 2024 data (30,274 flats completed).
notes: STATUS: DRAFT — MPs' bill, Chamber print 298/0, delivered to deputies 7 Sep 2026 (VeKLEP KORNDXQH9BRI, '3 - pripominkove rizeni ukonceno', comment window for the government's opinion closed 2026-09-17). No RIA (MPs' bill); the problem statement is the důvodová zpráva, section 1.3: 'Potřeba navrhované právní úpravy vychází z absence přímého motivačního kritéria pro bytovou výstavbu v platném systému rozpočtového určení daní.' DATES: proposed effect 1 January 2028 ('Tento zákon nabývá účinnosti dnem 1. ledna 2028'); CZSO passes floor-area totals to MF by 31 May each year; MF issues the amounts by decree effective 1 September, first for 2028 (flats first used in 2027); Prague passes 3,000 CZK/m² to the city district within 30 days. Rates: 3,000 CZK/m² (towns up to 10,000 inhabitants), 3,500 (10,000-50,000), 4,000 (50,000+), regions 500, Prague 5,000; caps of 200 m² per flat in a family house and 120 m² per other flat; data source CZSO survey Stav 7-99 fed from ISUI since 2025. Scale basis from the memorandum: 30,274 flats with 2,158,155 m² living area completed in 2024 (6,489 flats / 379,575 m² in Prague); 33,430 flats in 2025. Submitted by 16 deputies (first signatory Zdeněk Hřib); the government has not yet given its opinion, so passage is uncertain. DEDUP: veklep-KORNDXQH9BRI (2026-09-19 ledger) is the metadata card; veklep-KORNDUGC6N75 is the annual RUD shares decree. No other record covers a housing incentive in tax sharing. Who is affected: all 6,250 municipalities and 13 regions, Prague districts, housing developers negotiating with towns, CZSO and MF.

title: Act 159/2026 Sb. — 'Odstoupit od smlouvy' withdrawal button for every Czech online distance contract from 2027
money_note: No money is attached; the act creates duties and offences, not spending.
summary: Act 159/2026 Sb., promulgated on 2 September 2026 and in force from 1 January 2027, transposes Directive (EU) 2023/2673 by adding section 1830a to the Civil Code: any business that concludes a distance contract with a consumer through an online interface must offer a prominent, always-available withdrawal button labelled 'Odstoupit od smlouvy', a confirmation step and a text confirmation of receipt. The act also bans dark patterns in online sales of financial services, rewrites pre-contractual disclosure for them and makes a missing button or confirmation a consumer-protection offence.
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — Act 159/2026 Sb. of 19 August 2026, 'kterým se mění některé zákony v souvislosti se smlouvami o finančních službách uzavíranými na dálku'; e-Sbírka ELI versions 2026-09-02 (promulgated) and 2027-01-01 (in force); read from the ELI open-data text fragments (opendata.eselpoint.gov.cz), payload regulation/esbirka/sb-2026-159.txt. On 2026-09-18 this number was still a 'právě digitalizujeme' stub (named gap of that pass). DATES: in force 1 January 2027 (Cl. XII: 'Tento zákon nabývá účinnosti dnem 1. ledna 2027'). Directive 2023/2673 set transposition by 19 Dec 2025 and application from 19 Jun 2026, so Czech application is about 6.5 months late. SCOPE: the new section 1830a sits in the Civil Code's general rules for distance and off-premises contracts (section 1820 info duty amended to name the button and its location), so it covers every e-shop and online service, not only finance, consistent with the directive's new Art 11a of Directive 2011/83/EU. Offences added to Act 634/1992 s. 24(16)(q)-(r) for a missing button or missing confirmation; s. 5e bans manipulative interfaces for distance financial services; CNB supervision annex updated. Also amends the consumer credit, payment services, insurance distribution, capital market, investment funds, PEPP, IZPP and digital-finance (MiCA white paper) acts. DEDUP: reg-dmfsd-distance-finance (EU directive, framed for financial services, dated 2026-06-19) records the EU instrument; veklep-KORNDP3EGBS2 is the withdrawal-form regulation 29/2023 update. This record is the Czech enactment with the national in-force date and the general e-commerce scope. Who must act: every Czech e-shop and online subscription seller, online lenders, insurers and investment apps, and their platform vendors (Shoptet, Upgates and similar).
quote: (1) Má-li spotřebitel právo odstoupit od smlouvy uzavřené distančním způsobem prostřednictvím on-line rozhraní, umožní podnikatel spotřebiteli odstoupit od smlouvy také prohlášením učiněným v on-line rozhraní použitím tlačítka nebo obdobného ovládacího prvku pro odstoupení od smlouvy.

title: New Union Customs Code, Reg. (EU) 2026/2108 — EU Customs Data Hub, e-commerce handling fee and importer duties from 2027
money_note: No money is attached in the regulation text; the per-item handling fee amount is left to a Commission delegated act.
summary: Regulation (EU) 2026/2108, published on 19 September 2026, replaces the Union Customs Code with a new code, creates an EU Customs Authority and an EU Customs Data Hub that will replace national customs systems, and applies generally from 21 September 2027. It introduces a fixed per-item Union handling fee on goods sold in distance sales, makes the importer for distance sales liable for duty after the end of the EUR 150 relief, and phases in the Data Hub from 1 March 2031 (voluntary) to 1 March 2034 (mandatory for all operators).
notes: STATUS: ENACTED — Regulation (EU) 2026/2108 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 16 September 2026, OJ L of 19 September 2026 (CELLAR SPARQL enumeration 2026-09-17..19, file regulation/eu/ojL-pub-2026-09-17_19.csv); full text via CELEX content negotiation (regulation/eu/32026R2108-en.html). It repeals Regulation (EU) No 952/2013. DATES (Art on entry into force and application): in force the day after publication (20 Sep 2026); 'This Regulation shall apply from 21 September 2027'; delegated and implementing powers, Art 20 (charges, except paras 1, 2 and 4) and other listed articles apply at once; Art 20(2) handling fee applies 10 days after the delegated act under Art 20(10) enters into force (recital: first delegated act to enter into force rapidly); Articles 41-45 and 74-75 and 78 (Data Hub processing, placement of goods, Trust and Check self-release) apply from 1 July 2028; recital: Data Hub voluntary use from 1 March 2031, fully developed and used by all operators by 1 March 2034. Recital 74: 'Eliminating the duty relief for the importation of goods with a value not exceeding EUR 150'. Art 78 lets Trust and Check traders release goods on customs' behalf; IOSS users must submit distance-sales data by the day after payment (Art 74(3)). Czech context: Generální ředitelství cel is already buying a low-value consignment app (ted-506865-2026) and a customs Single Window (ted-602015-2026); NKU found value discrepancies in 61% of checked e-commerce parcels (nku-dph-ecommerce). DEDUP: no record in the corpus carries the customs reform (searched signals for customs code, customs authority, data hub, deemed importer, EUR 150, IOSS on 2026-09-19). Who must act: every Czech importer and exporter, customs brokers, forwarders and express carriers, e-shops and marketplaces selling into the EU from third countries, customs-software vendors.
quote: By way of derogation from paragraph 1, customs authorities shall collect a Union handling fee of a fixed amount per item for the services to be rendered for handling a request for placing goods under the release for free circulation procedure where those goods are sold in distance sales.

title: EU tariff suspensions evaluation — review of autonomous tariff suspension and quota scheme
summary: The European Commission will evaluate the industrial and agricultural autonomous tariff suspensions and quotas scheme. It will assess whether the objectives of Communication 2011/C 36/02 were met and whether the scheme remains fit for purpose.

quote: Návrh zákona o podmínkách inovativního a škálovatelného podnikání a o změně některých dalších zákonů — Návrh je do legislativního procesu předkládán na základě usnesení vlády č. 175/2026 ze dne 23. března 2026, který byl schválen Plán legislativních prací vlády na zbývající část roku 2026.
title: Innovative and scalable business act — CZ Industry Ministry bill in consultation
summary: The Ministry of Industry and Trade put out for inter-ministerial consultation a bill on the conditions for innovative and scalable business, amending other laws. It evidences a pending legal framework for innovative, scalable businesses.

title: Security forces medical fitness — draft amendment to Decree 226/2019
summary: A draft decree amending Decree 226/2019 on medical fitness for service in the security forces entered interministerial consultation. It evidences planned changes to health requirements for members of the security forces.

title: Professional pesticide application equipment — draft amendment to Decree 207/2012
summary: A draft decree amending Decree 207/2012 on professional equipment for applying plant protection products, together with related decrees on technical equipment and wooden packaging marking, entered interministerial consultation. It evidences upcoming rule changes for agricultural spraying equipment.

title: Driver training rules — draft amendment to Decree 167/2002 on driving qualification
summary: A draft decree amending Decree 167/2002, which implements the law on obtaining and improving professional competence to drive motor vehicles, entered interministerial consultation. It evidences planned changes to driver training and qualification rules.

title: Certification of copies and signatures — draft amendment to Decree 36/2006
summary: A draft decree amending Decree 36/2006 on certifying copies of documents and verifying signatures entered interministerial consultation. It evidences planned changes to how official document and signature authentication works.

quote: Návrh zákona, kterým se mění zákon č. 159/1999 Sb., o některých podmínkách podnikání a o výkonu některých činností v oblasti cestovního ruchu, ve znění pozdějších předpisů, a další související zákony — Materiál je předkládán v souladu s Plánem legislativních prací vlády na zbývající část roku 2026.
title: Tourism business law amendment — Ministry for Regional Development draft bill in consultation
summary: The Ministry for Regional Development put out for interministerial consultation a draft bill amending Act 159/1999 on certain conditions of business in tourism, together with related laws. It evidences upcoming regulatory change for Czech travel and tourism businesses.

title: 2026 travel allowance rates — draft amendment to the decree on reimbursement rates
summary: A draft decree amending Decree 573/2025, which sets the 2026 basic rate for using road vehicles, meal allowances and average fuel prices for travel reimbursements, entered interministerial consultation. It evidences a mid-year revision of statutory travel expense rates that employers must apply.
